**Observations from the image:**

- **Plant part affected**: Single leaf (upper surface visible), placed on a concrete surface
- **Leaf shape**: Normal tomato leaf shape, no distortion or shoestring appearance
- **Color pattern**: Overall dark green with distinct pale yellowish-green patches/spots scattered across the upper leaf surface
- **Lesion characteristics**: Diffuse, irregular yellowish areas with indistinct margins — no brown concentric rings, no fuzzy gray/white spore masses, no discrete dark spots with halos, no water-soaked greasy areas
- **Texture**: Normal leaf pubescence visible; no white powdery coating

**Differential reasoning:**

- **Early Blight / Late Blight**: No concentric ring lesions or brown papery tissue — ruled out
- **Gray Mold**: No gray-brown fuzzy sporulation — ruled out
- **Powdery Mildew**: No white powdery coating visible — ruled out
- **Bacterial Speck / Canker**: No discrete dark pinpoint lesions or bird-eye spots — ruled out
- **Cucumber Mosaic Virus**: Leaf is not distorted/shoestring-shaped and mosaic is not pronounced enough
- **Leaf Mold**: Matches well — pale greenish-yellow spots on upper leaf surface with indistinct margins, no definite lesion borders, older lower leaf showing earliest symptoms. Description: "brighter yellow with indistinct chlorosis on upper leaf surface" — consistent with what's visible here

The diffuse yellowish chlorotic patches with indistinct margins on an otherwise intact and normally shaped tomato leaf most closely match **Leaf Mold** (early/upper-surface phase).
